backlog.spec: Replace standard LayerNorm with a LayerNorm that applies a learnable scalar weight and bias to the pre-normalization values, normalized by their squared Euclidean norm plus epsilon. backlog.spec: Modify the Adam optimizer to update level parameters (first and second moment estimates) at a rate different from model parameters. Specifically, apply a boosted learning rate to the moment estimates themselves, allowing them to track gradients more closely while retaining convergence stability.

backlog.spec: Apply weight decay only to parameters whose magnitude exceeds a threshold during the update step. This prevents decay from corrupting already large weights that are less sensitive to regularization.
backlog.title: Clipped Weight Decay

backlog.spec: Update the learning rate optimization during training so that the weight of the parameters in the Adam parameter space is the reciprocal of their magnitude in the prior space. This effectively allows the Adam optimizer to step closer to the global optimum by altering its parametrization.
backlog.title: Reciprocal Grad Scaling (RGS)

backlog.spec: Insert a residual block before the final pre-norm linear layer that adds the output of the layer to its input (residual connection), before the pre-norm step. This increases the ability of layers to learn complex transformations.

backlog.spec: Add an 'Option' field to every normalization layer (e.g., LeftNorm, RightNorm) that applies a learned multiplier to the normed output. This allows the model to learn how much contribution to give to the normed output.

backlog.spec: Introduce a dynamic learning rate schedule where the learning rate is scaled by the reciprocal of the step number plus a constant factor, allowing for better early convergence and stability.
backlog.title: Dynamic Scaling Schedules

backlog.spec: Replace the standard attention mechanism with an invertible attention layer that computes the attention weights via an invertible matrix, allowing for exact reconstruction of the original input.
backlog.title: Invertible Layers

backlog.spec: Apply weight decay only to the weights of the current batch being processed, rather than the global model weights. This reduces the regularization effect and allows for more fine-grained learning.
backlog.title: Batch‑Specific Weight Decay

backlog.spec: Replace standard BatchNorm with an Adaptive BatchNorm that uses a learnable scale and shift parameters on top of the normalized features. This allows the model to learn which parts of the input should be scaled.
backlog.title: Adaptive Batch Norm

backlog.spec: Instead of pre-normalized inputs to GELU, apply a learnable, layer-wise scale-and-shift normalization after the Q/K/V projections, winning a remaining activation bump without extra multiplications. This effectively makes the GELU non-linear while keeping the attention economic.
backlog.title: Elastic Activation Normalization (EAnorm)

backlog.spec: Modify Adam's moving average of first moment not to decay at a constant rate, but with a per-layer schedule that starts at 1.0, decays linearly, and bottoms out at 0.5 by the final epoch for smaller layers, boosting early convergence stability.
backlog.title: Layer-Wise Adaptive Momentum (LAM)

backlog.spec: Allocate 10-2000 seconds of the 300s budget to a heavy pre-phase warmup schedule, extending from 0.004 to 0.001 linearly, then quickly ramping up to 0.0004 by the end. This simulates slower, more stable optimization.

backlog.spec: Split the input batch into high-frequency (top 500 tokens in embedding space) and low-frequency (remainder) sub-batches; train the high-freq subs with larger batch size per device, with low-freq sharing the rest, to test stability on hard tokens.

backlog.spec: Apply a learned GELU to the Q/K/V projections, followed by a learned Skew in the matrix multiplication to rescale the projection values, and then pass this to the attention kernel. This could allow for better attention brain integration.

backlog.spec: Use a class-based loss weighting (e.g., using the top 10% loss class as the anchor) to adjust the loss based on class frequency, giving more attention to the high-freq tokens.
backlog.title: Adaptive Loss Weighting (ALW)

backlog.spec: Add a dropout mask per the attention rank (1, 2, 3, or 4) which reduces the attention score for lower-ranked heads based on the current layer, optimizing the high-rank heads for better attention
backlog.title: Attention Dropout with Rank (ADR)

backlog.spec: Add an L2 regularization term to the gradient history of the optimizer (past G) at the end of each epoch, to force the optimizer to always stay close to the zero manifold for better generalization.
backlog.title: L2-Regularized Gradient History (LRGH)

backlog.spec: Scale the warmup ratio per token based on the embedding magnitude: tokens with large embedding values get a larger warmup fraction to receive more attention, while small tokens get smaller warmup fraction.
backlog.title: Frequency-Scaled Warmup (FSW)

backlog.spec: Normalize the input data X in each batch, before passing it to the projection matrices, so that each token is centered in the embedding space. This normalization can lead to better attention patterns by ensuring tokens are closer to the mean prior to attention.
